'''Jeanne A. Hardy''' is an American professor of biological and biophysical chemistry at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst|University of Massachusetts, Amherst.]] Her group's work is best known for designing [[Allosteric regulation|allosteric]] binding sites and control elements into human [[protease]]s.

== Education ==
Hardy received her B.S. and M.S. from [[Utah State University]] in 1994, working with Professor [[Ann Aust]] on [[bioinorganic chemistry]] projects relating to protein binding of iron and asbestos.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hardy|first1=Jeanne A.|last2=Aust|first2=Ann E.|date=January 1995|title=Iron in Asbestos Chemistry and Carcinogenicity|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=95|issue=1|pages=97–118|doi=10.1021/cr00033a005|issn=0009-2665}}</ref> She received a Ph.D. in 2000 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], working with Prof. [[Hillary C.M. Nelson]] on the structure of [[Heat shock protein|Heat Shock Transcription Factor]], which plays various roles as a molecular chaperone and an immune stimulant.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/roles-of-heat-shock-proteins/|title=Roles of Heat Shock Proteins|work=Scientific American|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Her postdoctoral work was undertaken at [[Sunesis Pharmaceuticals]] with [[National Academy of Inventors]] member and [[University of California, San Francisco|UCSF]] professor James "Jim" Wells, who told her how to invent tethering.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pharmacy.ucsf.edu/news/2015/12/wells-named-fellow-national-academy-inventors|title=Wells named a fellow of National Academy of Inventors {{!}} School of Pharmacy {{!}} UCSF|website=pharmacy.ucsf.edu|date=18 December 2015 |access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hardy joined the University of Massachusetts in 2005. She built a research program upon the biophysics of human proteases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=111522|title=Chemist Jeanne A. Hardy to Give Talk at Brookhaven Lab on Caspases, Causative Factor in Neurodegenerative Diseases, 4/24 {{!}} BNL Newsroom|website=www.bnl.gov|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> Her research focuses especially on [[caspase]]s, apoptotic proteins involved in the regulation of cell death, and with impacts in conditions such as Alzheimer's<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cies.org/grantee/jeanne-hardy|title=Jeanne Hardy {{!}} Fulbright Scholar Program|website=www.cies.org|access-date=2018-10-28}}</ref> and Parkinson's Disease.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dagbay|first1=Kevin B.|last2=Hardy|first2=Jeanne A.|date=2017-09-01|title=Multiple proteolytic events in caspase-6 self-activation impact conformations of discrete structural regions|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=114|issue=38|pages=E7977–E7986|doi=10.1073/pnas.1704640114|pmid=28864531|pmc=5617271|bibcode=2017PNAS..114E7977D |issn=0027-8424|doi-access=free}}</ref> Hardy's research group has determined allosteric regulation of caspase-6 selectively by zinc,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Velázquez-Delgado|first1=Elih M.|last2=Hardy|first2=Jeanne A.|date=2012-10-19|title=Zinc-mediated Allosteric Inhibition of Caspase-6|url=http://www.jbc.org/content/287/43/36000|journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=287|issue=43|pages=36000–36011|doi=10.1074/jbc.M112.397752|issn=0021-9258|pmid=22891250|pmc=3476268|doi-access=free}}</ref> mutation-based regulation of caspase-7,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hardy|first1=Jeanne A.|last2=Wells|first2=James A.|date=2009-07-06|title=Dissecting an allosteric switch in caspase-7 using chemical and mutational probes|journal=Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=284|issue=38|pages=26063–9|doi=10.1074/jbc.M109.001826|issn=0021-9258|pmid=19581639|pmc=2758006|doi-access=free}}</ref> and lead molecules against heat shock and multiple other cysteine proteases. Purportedly for this work, she was awarded tenure in 2012, and promoted to Full Professor in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.umass.edu/chemistry/faculty/jeanne-hardy|title=Jeanne Hardy {{!}} Department of Chemistry {{!}} UMass Amherst|website=www.umass.edu|access-date=2018-10-28|archive-date=2019-05-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505063226/http://www.umass.edu/chemistry/faculty/jeanne-hardy|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Awards ==

* 2018 - Inaugural Mahoney Prize in the Life Sciences<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cns.umass.edu/research/mahoney-life-sciences-prize|title=Mahoney Life Sciences Prize|website=www.cns.umass.edu|access-date=2018-10-28|date=2017-07-07}}</ref>
* 2014 - [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholar]], Paris, France
* 2009 - [[Eli Lilly and Company|Lilly]] Teaching Fellowship
* 2008 - [[Research Corporation|Cottrell Scholar Award]]
* 2003 - NIH Postdoctoral Fellow
* 2000 - [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science|JSPS]] Postdoctoral Fellow
